title: Buttons and text inputs with full state and semantics contracts
asA: user interacting with actions and text entry
iWant: controls that respond visibly and predictably in every state
soThat: I always know what is pressable, what is busy, and what went wrong

acceptanceCriteria.description: Buttons render all applicable states from the token layer: default, hover, focus, active, and disabled, each visually distinct per assets/component-specs.
acceptanceCriteria.then: each state is visually distinct and token-driven in both themes

acceptanceCriteria.description: A button driving an async action shows a busy state, suppresses duplicate submission while pending, and communicates the busy state to assistive technology.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a button wired to an async action
acceptanceCriteria.then: it enters busy state, ignores repeat activation, and exposes the state programmatically

acceptanceCriteria.description: Destructive-variant buttons are visually distinct via the danger tokens and never the default focused action in confirmation dialogs.
acceptanceCriteria.then: initial focus rests on the non-destructive action

acceptanceCriteria.description: Text inputs and textareas render default, focus, disabled, error, and success states from the token layer with a visible focus indicator.
acceptanceCriteria.then: each state is distinct, and focus is visible per spa-REQ-019

acceptanceCriteria.description: Inputs pair a programmatically associated visible label; placeholder text is never the only label.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the name comes from an associated label element or equivalent, not placeholder

acceptanceCriteria.description: Error state on an input pairs the danger border and icon with error text tied via aria-describedby and aria-invalid.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the message is programmatically associated and announced

acceptanceCriteria.description: Textareas resize within declared bounds without breaking layout, and long input never overflows the control.
acceptanceCriteria.when: content is entered and the control resized
acceptanceCriteria.then: layout holds and content scrolls within the control

acceptanceCriteria.description: Disabled controls are excluded from Tab order, expose their disabled state programmatically, and still meet the 3:1 non-text contrast for their boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are skipped by Tab, announced as disabled, and remain perceivable
